title: Parker Solar Probe, the fastest thing we've built
hook: A spacecraft skimming the Sun hit about 690,000 km/h, faster than anything else built.
peek: NASA's Parker Solar Probe flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere. At its closest passes, in late 2024 and 2025, it reached about 690,000 km/h, the fastest speed of any object people have made, while a heat shield kept its instruments near room temperature.
lede: Launched in 2018, NASA's Parker Solar Probe was built to do something no spacecraft had done: fly through the Sun's corona, its outer atmosphere. On 24 December 2024 it passed about 6.1 million km from the Sun's surface, moving at about 690,000 km/h. That is fast enough to go from New York to Tokyo in under a minute.

bullets.opening: Why reaching the Sun is hard
bullets.text: Earth carries everything on it around the Sun at about 30 km per second. To fall inwards, a spacecraft must cancel most of that sideways speed, which takes more energy than leaving the Solar System. Parker used seven flybys of Venus to brake.

A carbon foam shield about 11 cm thick faces the Sun at temperatures near 1,400°C. Behind it, the instruments stay close to room temperature, and the craft steers itself to keep the shield pointed the right way.
In April 2021 the probe crossed into the corona for the first time, the first spacecraft ever to do so. NASA described it as touching the Sun.

The probe is named after Eugene Parker, who predicted the solar wind in the 1950s when many doubted it. It was the first NASA spacecraft named after a living person, and he watched its launch at the age of 91.
